key_facts: the brown old seaman with the sabre cut first took up his lodging under our roof
“Fifteen men on the dead man’s chest-- Yo-ho-ho, and a bottle of rum!”
he threw down three or four gold pieces on the threshold
promised me a silver fourpenny on the first of every month if I would only keep my “weather-eye open for a seafaring man with one leg”
the Dry Tortugas, and wild deeds and places on the Spanish Main
calling him a “true sea-dog” and a “real old salt”
One of the cocks of his hat having fallen down, he let it hang from that day forth
The great sea-chest none of us had ever seen open.

forbidden_claims.claim: The captain promised the boy a golden sovereign twice yearly.
The one-legged seafaring man was searching for the captain to reward him.
The captain kept his sea-chest unlocked and open on the table for guests to see.

notes: The narrator fears the one-legged man on the captain's behalf, not the reverse; the sea-chest is explicitly never seen open.
